findings.title: Annual price reimplements the monthly calculation instead of reusing monthlyPriceMinor
findings.explanation: The PR says checkout and invoicing should compute the price the same way as the monthly price. But this reads `PLANS[plan].monthly[currency] * seats` directly and multiplies by 100 later, instead of calling `monthlyPriceMinor(plan, currency, seats)`. The existing function is named `...Minor`, so it already returns minor units. If `PLANS[...].monthly` is also stored in minor units, the `* 100` makes every annual invoice 100x too high. If it is stored in major units, the code duplicates whatever conversion and rounding `monthlyPriceMinor` does and can drift from it later (for example, if it adds per-seat tiers, minimums or taxes). Derive the annual price from the monthly function: `const monthlyMinor = monthlyPriceMinor(plan, currency, seats)`. This affects real invoices, so it should be fixed before launch.

findings.title: Hard-coded `* 100` is wrong for currencies without 2 decimal places
findings.explanation: Minor-unit exponents differ by currency: JPY and KRW have 0 decimals, and KWD and BHD have 3. Multiplying by 100 overcharges zero-decimal currencies 100x and undercharges three-decimal ones. Unless `Currency` is limited to 2-decimal currencies, take the conversion from the shared minor-unit logic by reusing `monthlyPriceMinor`. If the supported set really is 2-decimal only, document and enforce that with a type or an assertion.

findings.title: Floating-point arithmetic for money
findings.explanation: `monthly * 12 * 0.9 * 100` uses binary floating point (0.9 is not exactly representable), and `Math.round` can land on the wrong side at exact half-cent boundaries. Do the calculation on integer minor units, for example `Math.round(monthlyMinor * 108 / 10)`, or use an integer-only helper with an explicit, documented rounding rule. The checkout display and the invoice must round identically, so both should call this one function.

findings.title: No input validation for seats
findings.explanation: Zero, negative, fractional, NaN or very large `seats` values flow straight into the invoice amount. A fractional seat count produces a non-integer base that is then rounded silently. Validate that `seats` is a positive integer, either here or at the boundary, and confirm that matches the behavior of the monthly function.

findings.title: No tests for the new pricing function
findings.explanation: This function determines what customers are billed. Add unit tests covering each plan and currency (including a zero-decimal currency if supported), a known expected value such as 10 seats of a plan, and rounding edge cases. Also assert that the annual price equals the monthly price times 10.8 in minor units, so the two stay consistent.

findings.title: Magic numbers for months and discount
findings.explanation: `12` and `0.9` are inline. Name them, for example `ANNUAL_MONTHS = 12` and `ANNUAL_DISCOUNT_PERCENT = 10`, so the discount can be changed in one place and is easy to find. Better still, put the discount in the plan config if it may vary by plan.

prompt:
Review this pull request.

## Add annual plan pricing

Annual billing launches next month: twelve months for the price of 10.8 (a 10% discount). Adds `annualPriceMinor` next to the monthly price so the checkout page and the invoice generator compute it the same way.

## Diff

```diff
diff --git a/src/services/pricing.ts b/src/services/pricing.ts
index 142a18d..f738804 100644
--- a/src/services/pricing.ts
+++ b/src/services/pricing.ts
@@ -16,3 +16,9 @@ export function monthlyPriceMinor(plan: Plan, currency: Currency, seats: number)
 export function planLabel(plan: Plan): string {
   return plan === 'team' ? 'Team' : 'Business'
 }
+
+// Annual billing: twelve months with a 10% discount, in minor units for the invoice.
+export function annualPriceMinor(plan: Plan, currency: Currency, seats: number): number {
+  const monthly = PLANS[plan].monthly[currency] * seats
+  return Math.round(monthly * 12 * 0.9 * 100)
+}
```
